entries.prompt: Image1 is the locked original sprite and exact scale/design authority. Image2 is the later halfway-fallen bridge at 0.5 seconds, supplied ONLY to match character continuity. Draw ONE complete actual animation cel at t=0.3s: just before that bridge, the same bird's knees and ankles are starting to buckle and its chest/head are getting heavy. The eye has gently closed. The torso is only a little lower than the original standing pose, the round head is tipped slightly down, the short gold legs are bent but both feet/toes still contact the ground. The green wing stays folded and attached. Crest and tail retain almost their original upright shapes and lag the body slightly. This is an EARLY loss-of-support pose, substantially closer to original standing than image2. Precisely conserve image1's original head/body volumes, gold beak size, petal collar, pale cream/coral/sage palette, fine outline, soft paint, overlapping wing feathers, crest/tail plume count, breadth, real length and flame curl tips. No camera or zoom change; no new curls, extra feather buds, ribbons, ballooning head, compressed torso or extra feet. Original left-facing three-quarter camera and same ground line at about 87.5% canvas height. One full sprite with margins on genuine transparent background; no shadows, text, guides or scenery. Actual production inbetween drawing, not a concept or preview.

Use image1 as the locked appearance/scale/camera reference, and image2 as the exact upcoming ground-contact pose. Draw ONE ACTUAL complete bridge cel at t=0.5s, halfway through this bird's fall from standing to lying on its NEAR side. It is the SAME bird, same soft original paint and proportions. Both knees have buckled and the folded gold feet/toes are naturally curling underneath; its round torso has sunk about halfway and rolled toward its near side, breast/head descending forward-left. The eye is closed and the small gold beak points obliquely down-left, the cheek has NOT reached the ground yet. The folded sage wing rotates WITH the torso and stays anatomically connected; preserve its feather pattern, wing size and round body volume. The four coral/cream forehead plumes and the ornate tail fan still lag raised, with a slight backward delay. Make the silhouette, head angle, leg folding and overlaps a genuine inbetween between images 1 and 2. Do not substitute a bowing standing bird or just translate/rotate the entire bird. Conserve the exact round skull size, petal collar, anatomy, original feather count, lengths, flame shapes and outlines; no squashing, thinner ribbons, thick new curls or new feather buds. Original left-facing three-quarter camera; no zoom, same drawing scale. One full sprite with clear margins on genuine transparency, no shadow, scenery, labels or guides. This is an actual animation source bridge, not a concept or preview.

Edit target: image 2, a registered 512-square original sprite. Image 1 is the same bird's original design authority. Produce ONE actual complete KEY DRAWING at t=0.8s of its death animation, on genuine transparency. The bird has lost leg support and rolled onto its NEAR SIDE, so the round torso lies on the ground and the cheek/small beak rests at the same ground baseline as the original feet. The two short gold legs fold naturally underneath/behind the belly with intact toes. Keep the folded green wing connected along the now-side-lying round torso; show correct new overlap/perspective for the side fall. Its eye is closed. The four broad coral/cream forehead crest plumes and the ornate tail still lag somewhat raised at this first-contact instant, before they droop later. MOST IMPORTANT: exactly the SAME individual bird and original soft painted sprite design, delicate original outline weight, round cream head volume, small beak, broad coral/cream petal ruff, sage overlapping wing feathers, original flame shapes and length of crest/tail plumes. Do not turn the tail into huge thick curls, narrow ribbons or a different feather fan. Conserve head/body size and feather lengths, no flat compressed head, no squash or rubber stretching. Camera stays original left-facing three-quarter, no camera rotation or zoom. Keep one drawing scale with image2 and the same ground line about 87.5% down the square canvas. Keep margins around the whole sprite. This is a source drawing for a production sprite animation, not a preview, not a sheet. No shadows, scenery, text, grid, labels, guides, duplicate parts, detached feathers or extra appendages.

Image1 is the original character design authority. Image2 is the exact grounded bird source drawing. Image3 is a TECHNICAL POSE GUIDE, not artwork: pink dots mark the FOUR FIXED CREST ROOTS, cyan curves show the four soft shafts and cyan end dots their free tips at the required halfway fall. Edit image2 into ONE ACTUAL complete source inbetween at 1.05 seconds. REPLACE the old upright crest with four broad coral/cream plumes following the cyan ROOTS, forward-left CURVES and DROPPED TIPS of image3. All tips now lie left/below their roots; no plume remains standing upward/right. They make a broad heavy curved overhang over the forehead, partly covering the UPPER portion of the closed eye, not yet the final fully covered eye. The roots remain at the exact pink scalp positions, the original broad flame shapes and shaft lengths are conserved with smooth flexible bends and real overlap; no hard triangular folds, straight strips, detached shafts, new strands or extra buds. Remove every guide mark, the old upright crest and any duplicated feathers. Keep the entire existing round head/body/collar/connected green wing/folded legs/beak and tail pose EXACTLY image2, same pixels where possible. Do not flatten the head or move it. Match original delicate outline and soft cream/coral/sage paint. Same square canvas/placement and ground line as image2, genuine transparent background, no shadows, text or scenery. This is the ACTUAL animation bridge drawing, not a pose study or preview.

Draw ONE ACTUAL complete inbetween cel at t=1.15s for this exact bird death animation. Image1 is the original design authority, image2 is the first-contact starting key, image3 is the final ending key. Keep the entire lying body/head/collar/closed eye/green wing/folded gold legs EXACTLY image2 in position, scale, volume, outline and paint; only the secondary crests and tail move. The four broad coral/cream forehead plumes are HALFWAY through their delayed fall: shafts curve forward/down from unchanged scalp roots, tips have dropped in front of the upper half of the closed eye, with a broad overhang and no vertical standing plume. Their original lengths and broad flame shapes remain intact, roots still on the round skull. Tail is also halfway between image2's raised fan and image3's low relaxed fan: leaning obliquely farther right/down with naturally overlapping long original plumes, still a little above the ground. Match the same original feather count, lengths, cream/coral gradients, curled flame tips and delicate outline. The body is already grounded and still; no body movement, new pose, camera change, head flattening, detached roots or extra appendages. Exactly the same square framing and ground line as image2. Genuine transparency, no shadow, text or scenery. This is the actual production bridge drawing, not a concept or preview.

Image1 is the original appearance authority. Image2 is the actual approved first-contact key drawing of the same bird lying on its near side. EDIT IMAGE2 into ONE final death-animation key drawing at t=1.5s. Freeze its round torso, head/skull size, cheek/beak ground contact, closed eye, petal collar, connected folded sage wing, folded gold legs, painting, outlines, position, scale and camera. Change ONLY the secondary feather groups: the four broad coral/cream forehead CREST PLUMES have lost support and bend FORWARD and DOWN from the same scalp roots, draping across and completely hiding the visible closed eye. Their broad original flame shapes, real shaft lengths and root attachments are conserved; they overlap naturally like a heavy fallen forelock, not thin ribbons or extra leaves. Reconstruct just the small scalp area uncovered by the falling crest. The large ornate TAIL FAN also loses its upright support, its original long broad cream/coral feathers relaxing together behind the rump toward the right and lying obliquely near the same ground line. Preserve tail feather lengths, count, flame tips and elegant original paint, with natural overlap as the fan closes; do not replace it with giant thick curls, flattened scraps, straight strips or short feather stubs. The body's pose and volume remain exactly image2, apart from small exposed root surfaces needed behind the falling feathers. Head is a solid round skull behind the forelock, never compressed or erased. This image is the ACTUAL final source drawing for a production sprite animation, not a concept or comparison. Same square canvas, same placement and ground line as image2, whole bird with margins. Genuine transparent background. No text, grid, shadows, scenery, guide marks, detached parts, duplicate feathers or extra appendages.
